subject: Post-call: Performance SLO & concurrency follow-up / Redwood rate limits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ethan.park@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Performance SLO & concurrency follow-up

Hi Alex / team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great discussion and really helpful context on Nimbus' production traffic patterns. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of requirements (from call):
- P95 latency target: <= 250ms for streaming endpoints (end-to-end for median prompt sizes)
- Average request: ~1.2k tokens (prompt+response) with streaming enabled for UX
- Steady-state throughput target: ~400 requests per second (RPS) sustained
- Peak/burst parallel requests: up to ~1,200 concurrent in short bursts (1-5 minutes)
- Connection pooling: long-lived keepalives from a pool of ~500 client connections across our fleet

Redwood baseline constraints / negotiation points:
- Hosted defaults: account-level concurrency quota 200 concurrent requests and soft rate limits ~300 RPS.
- Options we discussed: Dedicated reserved capacity (predictable throughput), burst-capacity add-on, or hybrid approach (dedicated baseline + burst).

Proposed path from Redwood to support Nimbus pilot:
1) Pilot configuration: Guarantee 800 concurrent baseline (reserved) with burst allowance to 1,200 for 5-10 minute windows.
2) Streaming optimization: Use continuous batching + prefix caching to meet the 250ms P95 — requires turning on streaming+chunk sizing for your client.
3) Connection guidance: Use HTTP/1.1 keepalives with a pool of 500 sockets; we recommend connection reuse to reduce handshake overhead.
4) Load validation: Please send the CSV load profile you mentioned (requests/sec by minute for a typical day + 95th-99th percentile bursts). We will run a staged soak test from our side.
5) Commercials: I will review internal pricing for reserved baseline vs. burst overage and get back with a proposal by EOD Thursday (4/22).

Next steps for you:
- Alex: send the full traffic profile and procurement contact (if different from the person on the call).
- Procurement: we’ll need a PO + standard security addendum for Dedicated if you choose that path.

Attaching: nimbus_concurrency_requirements.pdf (your doc from the call).

I’m looping in Laura and Ethan on the cc — Laura to review the SLO details and Ethan to validate the streaming approach for the pilot.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0189

Attachment: nimbus_concurrency_requirements.pdf (application/pdf, 86 KB)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLO & concurrency follow-up

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. That matches our notes. A couple quick clarifications and asks so we can move to procurement: 

1) Can you confirm the guaranteed baseline concurrency (800) and the exact burst window you recommend (5 vs 10 minutes)? We need the written quota to include burst duration for our SRE runbook.

2) Pilot pricing: we are OK with a short-term pilot but need a not-to-exceed number for the month of the pilot to share with procurement. Can you provide pilot pricing today or tomorrow?

3) Security/compliance: small ask — can you confirm there will be audit logs for all inference requests and that data retention settings can be configured per our policy? If you need a contact on the security side, cc'ed procurement will loop in our security lead.

Sending the traffic profile and a short CSV with minute-level RPS for last week attachment now.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of ML Platforms | Nimbus Health
alex.johnson@nimbushealth.com

Attachment: nimbus_traffic_profile_20270414.csv (text/csv, 12 KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ethan.park@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Performance SLO & concurrency follow-up — internal

Looping you all in — Alex sent the traffic CSV and pushed for written quota + pilot pricing. Procurement is involved, so we'll need a clean MAM and a short pricing note. My thoughts: 

- Negotiation boundary: we can approve an 800 baseline concurrency on hosted with a burst to 1,200 for up to 10 minutes for the pilot, but only if we gate by a 30% uplift in pilot fee vs. standard hosted. If Nimbus wants lower pilot fees we should require a 3-month committed reserved contract.
- Streaming: Ethan — can you confirm the 250ms P95 is achievable with continuous batching + 8k-token chunking for their average 1.2k tokens? If not, what telemetry changes do you need?
- Logs/compliance: Vanessa — confirm we can expose request-level audit logs and retention controls for a dedicated/reserved customer; also confirm any extra procurement paperwork.

I'll draft the MAM + a short one-sheet that calls out the baseline/burst numbers + pilot T&Cs. If you approve by EOD, I'll send to Alex with attachments and a DocuSign link for the MAM.

Marissa

Attachment: redwood_rate_limits_v2.pdf (application/pdf, 42 KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ethan.park@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLO & concurrency follow-up — Pilot proposal and next steps

Hi Alex / Procurement — appreciate the quick turnaround and for sending the CSV. Attached is a short Mutual Action Plan (MAM) and the updated rate-limits one-pager. Key items summarized below: 

Redwood pilot proposal (written):
- Baseline concurrent quota: 800 guaranteed concurrent requests (reserved)
- Burst allowance: up to 1,200 concurrent requests for windows of up to 10 minutes, throttled by token-rate and global account RPS caps during sustained events
- Pilot duration: 30 days; not-to-exceed pilot fee: $15,000 (covers reserved baseline + burst insurance for the pilot month)
- Acceptance criteria: successful soak test achieving 400 RPS steady-state and handling at least one 1,000-1,200 concurrent burst with P95 <= 250ms for streaming endpoints
- Data & logs: request-level audit logs will be available; retention configurable to 90/180/365 days depending on package (we can provide SOC2 evidence and a tailored retention policy).

Next steps / ask list:
1) Procurement: please review the attached MAM_Nimbus_Health_v1.docx and sign via DocuSign if acceptable. DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/s/ABC123 (placeholder).
2) Alex: confirm you want Redwood to run the staged soak test (we'll schedule with Ethan).
3) Engineering: Ethan to own test plan and telemetry checklist; Laura to validate SLO targets before pilot kickoff.

If this looks good we can put the MAM in DocuSign and spin up a pilot cluster (expected lead time 3 business days after signed MAM + PO).

Thanks — looking forward to getting Nimbus into a pilot.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0189
